grand_strategy.reading:
Milei's Argentina trades strategic alignment for money: the USD 20bn US Treasury swap and the USD 20bn IMF programme keep the peso and the debt afloat, and the price is a trade deal with Washington, the Isaac Accords with Israel and loud alignment with Trump. The hedge is the China swap, renewed to 2031, and the grain trade Beijing buys, and the paradox is that the American rescue and the Chinese trade pull against each other. Within South America the Mercosur bloc and the friction with Lula limit how far Milei can go, while the Falklands claim stays alive in rhetoric without stopping the London relationship.

Update of 2026-10-16. Two things changed the picture. First, the swap was used and repaid (USD 2.5bn, January 2026), so the American lifeline is now more a political tie than a debt, while the IMF programme missed its reserves target and inflation is back above 33% a year; the money that bought the alignment is not yet buying stability at home. Second, the Falklands stopped being rhetoric: the September 2026 sanctions on Sea Lion, the 60 proceedings and the arbitration threat turn the claim into a live quarrel with London, with the Israeli investor and with the oil majors' compliance departments, at the moment Milei's approval fell to 34%. The neighbourhood has split: a right-of-centre arc (Chile, Peru, Colombia, Paraguay, Bolivia) is warm, Brazil and Mexico are not, and the Mercosur summit showed that Argentina wants a bloc it can leave in all but name. Where the card had Argentina as a client who pays in alignment, it is now a client who is spending the alignment on a cause of its own.

After the Brazilian runoff of 25 October 2026. Lula won a fourth term and Milei, who had campaigned openly for Flavio Bolsonaro, did not congratulate him: on 27 October his spokesman said the government takes note of the result and will not comment, while the right-of-centre presidents of Chile, Paraguay, Bolivia, Ecuador and Panama sent congratulations (MercoPress, Buenos Aires Herald, 26-27 October). Nothing in the week reverses the earlier reading: Argentina keeps the Mercosur membership it needs, the quarrel with Brazil is now a four-year fact rather than a bet on the election, and the ideological arc Milei wanted to lead does not follow him against Brasilia. Not changed this week: the EU-Mercosur interim agreement (provisional application since 1 May 2026, Court of Justice opinion pending; no newer item found) and the US relationship, where Trump questioned Lula's win without a formal White House statement and Milei stays on the same side.

Trend still warming in alignment, but the Falklands is a new strain: Trump has hinted at shifting Washington's neutrality towards Argentina and also refused to say whether the US would back the UK in a future conflict (Al Jazeera, 4 Sep 2026), which cuts in Milei's favour yet leaves the US formally neutral. Update 2026-10-29: after Lula's re-election Trump questioned the result, comparing it to the 2020 US election, with no formal White House statement, while Milei withheld congratulations; the two stand on the same side of the Brazilian result, but no joint act is sourced, so the trend is unchanged (MercoPress, 26 Oct 2026).
